experiments.why: A common f64 literal that f32 cannot hold exactly, so lo must carry a nonzero remainder.
Pi at full double precision split into an f32 hi word and its remainder.
2^24+1, the first integer f32 cannot hold, so hi is 16777216 and lo must be exactly 1.
A negative deep-zoom coordinate checks the sign of both words.
A large magnitude with fractional digits, where lo carries what the f32 hi word drops.
A value in the f32 subnormal range, where the remainder underflows to zero.
A value past the f32 maximum, where hi overflows to Infinity.
The slot the tests pin, which must come back as group 2, binding 5.
Pinning the guard at the first slot must still give one binding named _fp64.

obligations.statement: splitF64(x) returns [hi, lo] where hi equals Math.fround(x) and lo equals Math.fround(x - hi).

obligations.why: the quote is not inside a test in shader-dsl/src/core/passes/fp64-lower.test.ts that calls splitF64

obligations.statement: When a module that uses f64 arithmetic lists fp64Guard({ group: 2, binding: 5 }) in uses, fp64Lower places the _fp64 guard binding at group 2, binding 5.

source.quote: No duplicate injection alongside the pin.

obligations.statement: When fp64Guard pins the guard slot, the module fp64Lower returns has exactly one binding named _fp64, with no auto-injected duplicate.
